priyank766-opensource-skill-contributor-.description: Review of a first-time or early-stage contributor's pull request, where the technical bar stays fixed but the sequencing, batching, and supplied context change. Use when GitHub labels the author a first-time contributor, when the PR comes from a newcomer to this repo, when it arrives via Hacktoberfest, GSoC, Outreachy, or a good-first-issue, when the change is technically close but procedurally messy (missing DCO, wrong base branch, unsigned commits, failing lint), or when the PR must be declined and the decline needs to not cost the project a future contributor. priyank766-opensource-skill-contributor-.author: Priyank Patel

priyank766-opensource-skill-dependency-r.description: Supply-chain review of dependency and CI changes in an open-source pull request. Use when a PR adds or bumps a dependency, changes a lockfile, introduces a build or postinstall script, edits a GitHub Actions workflow, changes a container base image, or when a bot-generated dependency bump needs human judgement before merge. Covers install-time code execution, package-identity and typosquat checks, artifact provenance, transitive footprint, license class, and workflow privilege changes. Ecosystem-agnostic — npm, PyPI, Go, Cargo, RubyGems, Composer, containers. Do NOT use for routine patch…

priyank766-opensource-skill-docs-review.description: Review of documentation correctness in an open-source pull request — treating docs as unexecuted code and verifying them by running them. Use when a diff touches README files, docstrings, tutorials, quickstarts, API reference, migration guides, changelogs, or example projects, and equally when a code diff renames a symbol, changes a default, adds a required argument, or alters a config key in a way that silently invalidates documentation elsewhere in the repo. Verifies samples in a clean environment, walks quickstarts from an empty state, greps the docs tree for every symbol the diff touched,…

priyank766-opensource-skill-performance-.description: Performance and resource-efficiency review of an open-source pull request or diff. Use when the diff introduces I/O inside a loop, new database queries or query predicates, caching or invalidation changes, large allocations or whole-file reads, changes to a documented hot path, an algorithmic complexity change, a switch between streaming and buffering, or a mix of blocking and async code. Applies a measurement-first rule — every claim must be backed by a benchmark run on both base and head, except complexity-class regressions and unbounded resource growth, which are arguable from the diff…
priyank766-opensource-skill-performance-.author: Priyank Patel

priyank766-opensource-skill-pr-review.description: High-signal, maintainer-grade review of an open-source pull request. Use when asked to review a PR, review a diff, look over changes before posting feedback, or when preparing review comments for a GitHub pull request. Applies a weighted 10-point quality filter so only findings scoring 8.0+ are surfaced, and enforces a human contributor voice instead of AI cheerleading. Works for any language or ecosystem. Do NOT use for reviewing your own uncommitted work-in-progress.
priyank766-opensource-skill-pr-review.author: Priyank Patel

priyank766-opensource-skill-security-rev.description: Security-focused review of an open-source pull request or diff. priyank766-opensource-skill-test-review.description: Review of test quality in an open-source pull request, and of the tests the PR should have written but did not.
